operations.comment: ; Commentary round 005: all classified source reviewed; unknown spans stay verbatim.
; CPU execution view uses effective PRG 8 KiB banks [0,1,2,3]. Physical identity
; remains in region comments/review inventory. MMC1 writes can change live views.
; work0..work8 and pointer scratch are shared across subsystems, not stable variables.
; Actor arrays have seven entries. Fixed-point X/Y use three fractional bits.
; Names ending in a hardware address keep unresolved field meaning explicit.
; Alternate zero-page lifetimes during departure scenes and cell service.
; iNES header: mapper 1, 32 KiB PRG, 128 KiB CHR, no trainer; physical offsets include these 16 header bytes.
; Transfer the physical PRG start to the validated reset entry. This does not imply natural execution at $8000.

; Initialize cockpit state, palettes, nametables and OAM. Select the mission-parity graphics family, clear requests, spawn the three standard actors and synchronize rendering with NMI and sprite zero. The entry at $8007 preserves the message timer.
; Alternate initialization entry preserves the active message timer while rebuilding cockpit graphics and actors.
; Reset the mission clock and decode the starting map position. Clear objectives and failure, set heading 4 and speed $0500, then restart the spawn countdown.
; Restore resource $50ff, ammunition and signed status. Missions with the secondary-weapon flag receive three rounds instead of fifteen; the other ammunition counter is preserved on that path.
; Enable cockpit NMI work and rendering, clear warning history, then enter the two-part flight frame loop with the NMI latch armed.

; Update the little-endian mission countdown. At one remaining tick, start a 255-frame grace period and a message; countdown and grace handling are separate. The connected countdown, grace and spawn-reset continuations are now classified.
; Restart the spawn countdown after announcing clock expiry; continue into the clock decrement path.

; Handle failure and flight-mode conditions before the cockpit frame. Mode 2 decrements a signed 16-bit timer and dispatches timeout or negative-count cleanup. A negative condition can consume a life; timed-mode exits restore graphics before returning to flight.
; For mode zero, enter mode two, save the graphics family and select family two. Copy its palette, respawn cockpit actors and allocate types 16 through 18. Continue into the signed-timer checks.
; Restore the graphics family, start clock grace when time remains, run the mode-exit scene and restart cockpit initialization at its message-preserving entry.
; Clear the mission clock and grace, restore the graphics family and add 200 score units before normal cockpit processing.

; Check the signed auxiliary timer, then run the first cockpit frame half: spawn/update actors, wait for sprite-zero timing, select CHR, and synchronize on the NMI frame latch. Failure checks can consume a life. The two frame halves select different NMI work through cockpit_half.
; Return to the enclosing mission driver after the flight frame selects an exit.
; When the flight-limit flag is set, force a control bit and subtract 18 from the 16-bit speed if it is at least 20. This is a conditional drag effect, not a universal speed decay.
; Run the second cockpit frame half, synchronize rendering with sprite zero and NMI, then select the view-dependent CHR bank. Only a changed map cell enters the terrain/service tests below.

; Compare old/new map-cell directional bits with the 16-step heading. Disallowed crossings reverse heading. Cell type $10 selects rescue service. Its result commits the rescue/objective counters or consumes a life.

; Actor zero reports success as screen X=1. On success mark the map cell, increment the rescue counter and objective count, optionally show the objective-complete message, run departure service and award 100 score units. Failure consumes a life and enters the failure presentation.
; Consume a life, set failure_request and enter the common failure presentation.
; Cell type $20 disables NMI and enters base service; success marks the cell, increments the base counter, refills resources and runs departure.

; Run the base arrival, refill resources and inspect actor zero's result. Success marks the cell, increments the base counter, runs the interlude and departure service, then rebuilds the cockpit. Failure consumes a life. Counter names describe the now-established caller roles.
; Mark a type-$30 map cell with bit $40 on this transition. This transition initializes special flight mode, its timer and actor schedule; the exact original objective name remains uncertain.
; Enter mode one, show its message, initialize the special count and 140-tick timer, then schedule existing actors for the transition.

; Normal continuation jumps back to the cockpit update. The barrier branch clears fractional heading, adds a half turn modulo 16, and advances the world position through the heading-vector helper; then stops movement and recenters the map cell before testing objectives and the retry count.

; Stop movement and center world coordinates inside the current map cell. Show the barrier message. Continue flight while objectives remain and fewer than four attempts have accumulated; otherwise disable NMI and return result 2 to the mission driver.

; Raise the frame latch and consume pending palette/OAM requests. Request-specific continuations now include classified scene/service drawing callbacks. The latch is what foreground frame waits observe.
; Finish this NMI request by ticking sound and music and returning.
; Finish palette handling with the common sound/music tick.
; Advance scene animation, then tick sound and music for this NMI mode.
; Render the service sprites, reset the PPU address latch destination and tick audio.
; Upload the scene's background and sprite work, then tick audio.
; Select NMI duties by mode: 0 returns, $ff updates sound, 2 updates channel timers, 1 starts cockpit rendering, and other values transfer OAM. Reading PPUSTATUS also resets the PPU write latch.

; Select cockpit-half work: instrument upload, palette upload, or the indirect view drawing callback. Restore rendering flags, OAM, CHR selection and vertical scroll, then tick audio. The seven view callbacks are literal nametable writers selected through CockpitViewCallbackPointers.
; Clear the palette request and rejoin the rendering/scroll restoration shared by cockpit callbacks.
; Seven little-endian callback pointers indexed by view_index*2. Each points to a finite literal PPU-write body ending at the shared cockpit restoration routine.

; Set the flight-limit flag on empty resource, advance an 18-frame cadence, and trigger one-time warnings through bits 0/1 of the warning mask. The low-resource threshold is 18 on the high byte. Message and sound meanings are inferred only as warnings.
; Advance the variable warning cadence and select a sound by speed/limit state. A warning raises its cadence threshold by two up to 18. The zero/one periodic flag also requests the default alert.

; Scan actor occupancy, save previous controls, then latch both controllers. An auxiliary mode starts a signed countdown on input. A combined Select/Start-style mask enters the synchronized input-transition mode.
; Preserve the low control bits and replace the high nibble with a random value in 0..15 before storing the simulated controller state.
; Subtract ten from the little-endian resource counter and clamp both bytes to zero on signed underflow. The original quantity/unit is uncertain; the HUD also scales its high byte into a bar.

; Build actor sprites, delay if sprite allocation passes a threshold, and choose a drawing callback from the view-index table. The following entry integrates actor positions, applies controls and updates scroll/instruments. Unknown tail bytes are preserved.
; Sixteen four-byte heading records: signed little-endian dX then dY. AdvanceWorldPosition indexes by heading*4 and repeats the additions according to speed_high.
; Call the failure-transition setup; its following bytes and the adjacent uniform non-code block do not establish the complete failure presentation.
; Use sound-only NMI during the failure display. With no lives return result zero; otherwise rebuild the cockpit, refill resources and restart flight.
; Failure/lives presentation tile stream consumed by WriteSpriteTileStream. It crosses an older generic-data boundary; its final $ff sentinel is at $89c6.
; Forty zero-valued tile IDs inside the failure/lives sprite stream. The stream consumer continues through these bytes until its $ff terminator at $89c6; these are not an independent padding claim.
; The $ff terminator of the lives-presentation tile stream. The following byte begins executable screen setup.
; Load screen zero, fade its palette in, draw the lives indicator and a 7-by-8 sprite grid, wait about fifty frames and fade out. The palette helper uses a pointer in X/Y and a direction in A.
; Walk seven actor slots backwards. Types 9, 10 and 11 are either converted to type 3 or freed, depending on entry. These mechanical class numbers do not identify the original actor names.
; Preserve the top three packed bits and set pose bit 3 while clearing the low five bits.
; Restore the saved family, copy its 16 sprite colors, request palette upload, select its CHR bank and restore its metasprite pointer.
; Select sound-only NMI mode and enable NMI before the failure screen and timed sound presentation.
; Load screen ten, apply mission colors and enable the background. Play effect 15 twice separated by twenty frames, then wait eighty frames while channel timers advance.

; Load two signed 16-bit increments from the heading-indexed four-byte vector records. Repeatedly add them to world X/Y, with iteration count twice speed_high modulo 256 (zero runs 256 iterations). HeadingVectorDeltas supplies sixteen four-byte signed dX/dY records.
; Index the mission's two-byte accent record and replace palette-shadow colors $0212 and $0210.
; Choose a spawn descriptor and allocate an actor; return allocation result in X. Selection and allocation mechanics are explained at their helpers.

; Clear mode 2 if active, then walk eligible active actors. Skip types 2/3/5; types 9/10/11 take the special path. Award 20 or 10 decimal score units and increment the associated 16-bit counters by class; schedule behavior 3 and convert normal victims to type 3. Type 6 receives a position adjustment. Missing paths retain uncertainty about weapon/game meaning.
; Set the special count negative, restore cockpit graphics and add 200 score units.
; Increase lives up to nine and request the extra-life message and sound; then join area-effect processing.
; Finish the negative X offset using incoming carry, subtract 96 from fixed-point Y and select pose one while preserving unrelated packed bits.
; Clear the frame latch and PPU sprite-size selector before the synchronized controller press/release wait.
; Synchronize alternate frame halves with sprite zero while polling input. A press re-enters combined-button handling; release records a cleared prior control state before repeating the wait.
; Clear frame/size state, synchronize on NMI and sprite zero, then wait for input to change.
; Set grace to 255, clear the mission clock, request the clock message and restart the spawn countdown.
; Clear both mission-clock bytes and the grace counter.
; Reset spawn phase/high byte and set the low countdown to sixty.

; Strobe both standard controllers and rotate eight serial bits into separate bytes. Result layout is A=$80, B=$40, Select=$20, Start=$10, Up=$08, Down=$04, Left=$02, Right=$01. Both ports are polled, even where callers use only port 1.

; Convert the 16-bit scratch quantity to digit tiles, subtract tile-zero bias, and add into the six-digit score from right to left. Visible overflow digits subtract ten; carry propagates left into the preceding decimal digit. Score bytes themselves are decimal digits, not binary or packed BCD.
; Move left one digit, stop at the six-digit boundary, or increment the preceding digit before resuming decimal carry handling.
; Save Y/X, obtain a bounded random number below A, add the saved selector and call the text renderer with the saved base/bank arguments. Scratch pointers are reused by downstream routines.
; Hide all sprite slots, enable NMI/background, wait for vblank and reset the PPU address latch before applying PPU control/mask flags.

; Frame wait clears the NMI latch and spins until it is set. The delay entry repeats this Y times (Y=0 wraps to 256). The CHR helper forwards A through Y to the MMC1 bank routine; these are distinct callable entries.
; Foreground synchronization: NMI must be enabled and reach ServiceNmiRequests.

; Wait until both controllers are released, then poll once per NMI frame for at most the scratch counter. One entry sets a 200-frame timeout. Return A=1 for input, A=0 for timeout; the earlier entry can inherit the timeout byte.

; Two distinct routines disable rendering and choose a CHR bank before transfer. First reads count bytes from PPU source to CPU destination; second copies PPU source to PPU destination. Each read discards the buffered PPUDATA read, then consumes the actual byte; both pointers advance and the 16-bit count decreases to zero.
; PPU-to-PPU copy entry; destination is a PPU address rather than CPU memory.

; Compose PPUCTRL from NMI, background/sprite pattern selection, increment-by-32 and sprite-size flags. Boolean inputs add disjoint bit weights; callers must keep them in the intended zero/nonzero form. Nametable bits remain zero.
; Pack emphasis bits 0..2 and separate sprite/background/left-edge flags into PPUMASK. Reused scratch state is not an independent hardware register shadow.
; Poll PPUSTATUS bit 7 until set. The hardware read also resets the shared PPU write latch. This is a polling wait independent of the NMI frame latch.
; Poll PPUSTATUS until sprite-zero hit clears, then continue into the complementary hit wait. These waits require rendering to advance.
; Poll PPUSTATUS bit 6. Correct progress requires the sprite-zero rendering setup expected by the caller; this alone is not a frame wait.

; Three separate entries: DMA page $07 into OAM; upload two 16-byte palette shadows (mirroring the first color); write one OAM record from sprite scratch values using index*4. Palette upload finishes by resetting PPU address to zero.
; Palette upload entry; palette shadows are CPU RAM and not physical ROM identities.
; Sprite writer entry: Y,tile,attributes,X are stored in that order.
; Set Y and X coordinates for seven rows of eight OAM records, spaced eight pixels. Inputs X/Y give the top-left position; only coordinate fields are changed.
; Convert row Y and column X to an eight-column sprite index. Emit the tile bytes at work0/work1 until $ff, advancing the pointer with carry and preserving caller-supplied attributes.
; Emit the next non-$ff tile and advance the stream pointer, carrying into the high byte.
; Write offscreen Y=$f0 through the sprite-record helper for all 256 byte-index values, then wait for vblank and DMA the page. Indices wrap within the OAM page, so all 64 records end hidden.
; Select NMI mode zero and wait 80 frames. The following entry independently initializes the sprite grid.
; Write this view's literal nametable strips through PPUADDR/PPUDATA, reset the PPU address, then jump to shared cockpit restoration. Tile values are graphics IDs rather than text characters.
; Draw the second view's literal nametable strips, reset the PPU address and jump to shared cockpit rendering restoration.
; Draw the third view's literal nametable strips and rejoin the common rendering tail. PPU destination writes delimit the strips.

; Write four unrolled 32-tile rows at PPU $2880/$28a0/$28c0/$28e0. Most columns use tile $56 or $57, with a fixed $fe divider. Restore PPU address zero and join the common NMI rendering tail. Other literal view callbacks follow as independent entries.
; Write this view's literal nametable strips and rejoin shared cockpit restoration. The following callback entries use the same finite PPU-write format.
; Draw the sixth view's literal tile strips and rejoin the common rendering tail.
; Draw the seventh view's literal tile strips and rejoin the common rendering tail.

; Six sixteen-byte NES color records. The first is the cockpit background palette; subsequent records provide graphics-family and interlude sprite palettes. Selectors and partial pointer tables determine which record is used.

; A requests paired weapon latches only when both are idle. A rising B press consumes one secondary ammunition unit and either requests an area effect or latches a special projectile according to the stage table. Start increases 16-bit speed by 16, Select decreases it with zero clamp. A separate response accumulator rises by 100 while accelerating, otherwise falls by 100.
; A speed-indexed delay gates a seven-actor animation update while the flight mode is zero. Existing delay counts down; zero reloads from the speed table.

; Read a four-byte speed record for view limits and cadence. Move the view toward those limits, then process left/right controls: add/subtract fractional heading, wrap heading to 16 directions, shift actors horizontally and adjust view. With no turning request, ease the view toward center 3. The left-turn continuation subtracts $0060 from heading and advances view toward its upper bound.
; Unless a map message is active, subtract $0060 from fractional heading modulo sixteen. Outside special flight, increase view index toward its upper limit, then continue with right-input handling.

; Apply view-dependent descent to 16-bit altitude, then Up adds $0118 and Down subtracts $00fe. Clamp the high byte at zero or $69. These are internal units; HUD converts altitude_high*4 to decimal digits.
; Compute vertical scroll from altitude and throttle-response high byte, cap it at $ef, then propagate the scroll delta into actor Y positions.

; Repeatedly subtract five descending 16-bit decimal divisors and emit digit tiles through a destination pointer. Input is destroyed in scratch low/high; the five output positions use the digit-to-tile lookup. DecimalDivisors and DigitAndViewParameters retain the exact divisor and tile bytes.
; Five little-endian unsigned divisors: 10000, 1000, 100, 10, 1. The repeated-subtraction formatter consumes them from most to least significant.
; Stream digit_count bytes from the indirect tile buffer to PPUDATA. The following classified tables retain distinct decimal, digit and flight-parameter formats.

; Digit tile IDs followed by speed/view bounds, cadence and descent parameters. Indexed flight/instrument consumers establish the local fields; a single uniform record format does not describe this entire mixed block.

; Prepare three indicator tiles, update the map strip, format altitude/ammunition/speed, translate six score digits, and build a ten-cell resource bar. Speed is halved for display; altitude uses high byte times four. Resource fill uses 10-(resource_high>>3).

; Write remaining objective count (stage target minus accumulated count), indicators, map strip and numeric HUD buffers to fixed nametable addresses. Resource bars temporarily use PPU increment-by-32, then restore horizontal increment. Objective-count game semantics need confirmation from mission/service consumers.
; Instrument upload entry, distinct from the CPU-buffer formatting path above.
; Eight byte delays indexed by the bounded speed-derived animation selector.

; Multiply A by four, sign-extend the resulting byte, and add to Y of each nonfree actor except type 2. This is the implemented eight-bit wrap/sign behavior, not an unrestricted signed 16-bit multiplication.
; For each allocated actor except type 2, decrement the low three frame bits if nonzero. Upper bits share the same packed state byte.
; Skip directly to the next actor animation slot.

; Apply a signed horizontal shift to each allocated non-type-2 actor: positive input adds 16, negative input subtracts 16, with 16-bit position carry. Both signs propagate carry through the split position arrays.
; Finish the positive fixed-point X displacement using carry, then advance to the next actor.

; Alternate sprite allocation direction across frames, then scan seven active actors. Type plus animation-family offset selects a frame table; packed state chooses frame and bank. Convert fixed-point positions by dividing by eight; view-indexed perspective offsets modify displayed Y before metasprite emission. Type 2 bypasses the perspective adjustment.
; Hide OAM records from slot 3 onward. One entry sets descending allocation starting at 63, the other ascending allocation starting at 3. Slots 0..2 are reserved by other cockpit drawing.

; Resolve a frame pointer from the sprite-table base, then scan eight columns of three tiles. $ff cells are transparent. Clip transformed positions to X $40..$bf and Y $40..limit-1; allocate OAM until the direction-specific limit. Horizontal flip reverses column stepping and adds the tile/attribute flip adjustment. Tile IDs are doubled for 8x16 sprites. Optional left-edge clipping hides selected records.
; Perspective coefficient ramps and sprite attribute/offset fields used by the actor projection code. Coefficients are byte-quantized; no exact original generating formula is claimed.

; Thirty-five zero bytes in the perspective/parameter container. Indexed projection consumers and neighboring ramps were checked; the exact zero-tail meaning remains unresolved, so retain a generic data slice.

; Part of the pointer-backed eight-column by three-row actor metasprite payload. $ff denotes transparent cells. The thirty-two frame pointers select twenty-four-byte records across the adjacent preserved data boundaries.

; Thirty-five zero bytes in the perspective/parameter container. Indexed projection consumers and neighboring ramps were checked; the exact zero-tail meaning remains unresolved, so retain a generic data slice.
; Tail of the same twenty-four-byte actor metasprite record container. Keep physical boundaries independent of frame identities; the next byte starts an alternate random helper.

; Advance the byte LFSR (shift left, xor $1d on carry), then rotate a single set bit until it reaches the supplied limit and AND that bit with the new LFSR state. A rejected result re-enters at the limit store, changing the next bound. This differs from RandomBelowLimit, which builds a low-bit mask and retains its bound. Service uses the resulting LFSR low bit, not A; original intent of the unusual retry is uncertain.

; Build a mask covering the input limit, advance the byte LFSR (left shift, xor $1d on carry), mask the state and reject values >= limit. Return A and random_result below the requested bound. Bound zero is not a valid terminating contract. The following data and helper entries have independent classified boundaries.
; Unknown: Isolated $60 at $ad7d after the routine returns at $ad7c and before pose data. A standalone RTS stub and obsolete non-code residue remain competing interpretations. Retained verbatim.

; Eighteen little-endian frame pointers followed by fourteen twenty-four-byte pose records. Non-null pointers align to the payload record grid. Each record holds eight columns of three tile cells; $ff is transparent.
; Set the current actor's auxiliary byte to one; the next entry clears it. The flag's game meaning remains unresolved.
; Clear the actor auxiliary byte to zero; its shared predicate tests only zero versus nonzero.
; Return a carry-based predicate from the actor auxiliary byte: zero joins failure (carry set), nonzero joins success (carry clear). Game meaning of the byte remains unresolved.
; If the mission flag permits and the one-shot latch is clear, draw a value below 250 and select variant one for values below seventy. Preserve the script actor index across sampling.
; Convert actor fixed-point coordinates to pixels. Inside X [$56,$a6) and Y [$46,$96), decrement the shared signed status; return without changing it outside the window.
; Generate a fixed-point X displacement $0380+2*r with r<200 and add it to actors of types 9, 10 or 11. Restore the script actor index afterward.
; Continue the descending seven-slot special-actor displacement scan.
; Return the shared success predicate when the signed special counter is negative, otherwise failure.
; Increment the little-endian mission counter at $d3/$d4. Its exact displayed category remains uncertain.
; Add a random byte below script_arg2 to fixed-point actor X, preserving carry into the high byte.
; Add a random byte below script_arg2 to fixed-point actor Y. The random displacement is in fixed-point units.
; Use script_arg2 as the sound selector and preserve actor index X across the audio call. The following actor-scheduling helper has a separate entry.
; Queue behavior four for types 1 and 7; mark types 8 and 3 inactive. Iterate seven slots while preserving the scan index across queue calls.
; Mark type eight or three inactive while leaving other actor types unchanged.
; Restore the scan slot from the stack and continue through all seven actors.
; Fail if packed animation phase is five or greater; otherwise set actor type six and return the shared success predicate.
; Two callable entries add script_arg2/3 as a 16-bit delta to actor X or Y. No signed extension occurs here; the script provides both bytes.
; Set type three and pose one; mode two additionally forces the animation phase to seven. Following entries select type five or type six.
; Assign actor type five without changing its packed frame state.
; Assign actor type six and replace its pose bits with pose one while preserving the rest of packed frame state.

; Add separate script bytes to X/Y velocity (without propagating carry between components). A second entry packs a three-way horizontal pose based on signed X velocity into bits 3/4, preserving other packed-state bits.
; Return after applying the script velocity deltas.
; Choose horizontal velocity as floor(script_arg2/2)-random(script_arg2), then restore the script actor index. Following entries directly assign script_arg2 to X or Y velocity.
; Assign script_arg2 directly to the actor's signed horizontal velocity byte.
; Assign script_arg2 directly to the actor's signed vertical velocity byte.

; A first entry samples a symmetric-ish vertical velocity from a bounded random range. Following entries damp each signed component toward zero, then accelerate toward screen center X=$80,Y=$70. Both sign/carry continuations are classified and use the shared velocity-centering exits.
; Finish the negative horizontal acceleration step and continue with vertical centering.
; Finish the positive vertical acceleration step before the common return.

; Search active type-1/7 actors, also type 8 from mission 6 onward. Minimize Manhattan distance from screen point (ppu_sprite_pattern_high,$64); selected slot defaults to $ff and ties keep the earlier winner. Following predicate returns success only when a target exists.

; One entry calls the steering step four times. Each step damps both velocity components by two and accelerates them by four toward target fixed-point coordinates plus class-dependent offsets (mission_index/$40 or $46/$50 for type 8). Target slot must have been selected by the caller.
; Apply the second decrement on this negative horizontal steering path.

; Consume the low bit of a paired weapon request or test the special-projectile request. Shared predicate exits use carry clear for success and carry set for failure. Numeric latch meanings beyond their consumers remain uncertain.
; Clear the shared projectile request. Following predicates test screen X against $80, optionally requiring animation phase zero.
; Return success when actor screen X is below $80; otherwise return failure.
; Shared predicate ABI: carry clear means success; carry set means failure.
; Shared predicate failure exit.
; Succeed only when animation phase is zero and the actor's screen X is at least $80.

; Scan eligible targets, reject outside a coarse quarter-resolution 8-by-6 window, then use the frame collision bitmap to reject transparent cells. Award class-dependent score/counters, schedule hit behavior and convert victims to type 3; type 6 receives extra position/pose changes. Types 9..11 decrement the signed special counter. Accumulate any-hit flag and return the shared carry predicate. A type-5 source clears the special projectile latch.
; Increment the 16-bit class-specific hit counter before scheduling collision-hit behavior.
; A behavior-scheduling wrapper precedes this test. Divide fixed-point X/Y by eight and require X in [$20,$e0), Y in [$20,$a8). Shared predicate exits return carry clear when inside.
; Set X from script_arg2, or both X/Y from script_arg0/1, then shift unsigned coordinates left three into the split 16-bit arrays. Actor positions therefore use three fractional bits.
; Replace packed frame bits 3 and 4 with script_arg2 shifted left three. The script must supply a valid two-bit pose.
; Compose packed frame state as (script_arg1<<3)+script_arg0+$20. The arguments must satisfy the script record contract; this entry does not mask them.
; Increment the low three animation bits, saturating at seven. Return success on saturation and failure while advancing; preserve upper packed bits.

; Increment or decrement the low three bits of packed frame state. Increment overflow frees the actor; decrement underflow returns failure. On success preserve the upper five bits and return the shared predicate.
; Supply phase seven for the animation decrement underflow path.
; Set fixed-point Y to (80+floor(($ef-scroll)/2))*8 and X to (78+random(68))*8. Preserve the actor slot across sampling.
; Set fixed-point Y to (72 + floor((script_arg3-vertical_scroll)/2))*8 using 16-bit scratch arithmetic. The following score/name screen is a separate subsystem.

; Load CHR-backed working data, select sound-only NMI and wait for controller release before showing the score table. The RAM routine at $04f1 must return; its ROM upload origin is not established here.
; Synchronize on NMI, clear scroll and write the score-screen rendering registers directly.

; Preserve six score digits on the CPU stack, draw ten twelve-byte name/score rows, and insert a qualifying score. Six character slots use a cursor over the character grid; A selects, backspace removes a character, and Start/Select exits. Restore all six saved digits on every normal exit.
; Hide rendering, redraw palette/name/score rows and either enter name editing or the score-screen wait.
; Run the name-entry inactivity countdown, poll input and select character, backspace or exit behavior.
; Hide OAM, clear the displayed score digits and redraw the table after finishing or timing out the editor.
; Hide sprites, wait for Start/Select or the bounded timeout, then restore six saved score digits.

; Three sixteen-byte tables indexed by the controller direction nibble: signed horizontal destination delta, vertical destination delta and selected-character tile delta. The editor applies each move over four animation steps.
; Clear thirty rows of thirty-two tiles and the following sixty-four attribute bytes at PPU $2000.

; Compare six decimal digits against ten rows, shift each displaced twelve-byte name/score row, and copy the new score into its slot. Return Y as the insertion offset, with $78 indicating the terminal slot. The initial six stores target the same terminal byte; retain that behavior exactly.

; Disable NMI and read $0189 bytes from PPU $0b00 into CPU $03a3 using CHR bank 0. Copy a subset into the lower backup area. This CHR-backed data transfer is not evidence that CHR is only visual graphics.

; Rotate an eight-phase strip update when view cadence is active. Derive and clamp a local map window from world coordinates, index the 16-column cell grid, convert 14 cells to strip tiles, and place a heading sprite within the window. Marked cells may be suppressed by flight mode. A timed message overrides strip data; its classified continuation finishes the fourteen-cell loop and hides the heading marker.
; Copy the next message tile into the fourteen-cell strip buffer.
; Finish the fourteen-cell strip loop, hide its marker sprite and return.

; Sixteen heading sprite tiles, eight little-endian PPU destinations and forty-nine map-cell tile values. The map-strip consumers supply the selector domains; $ff entries are transparent/default markers where checked.
; Read the fourth byte of a four-byte mission record: upper nibble is world X and lower nibble is world Y, each shifted to a cell coordinate. Clear fractional position and set heading fraction four.
; Disable rendering, decode the starting cell and read 240 bytes from the mission's CHR bank/address into world_map_cells.

; Use upper nibbles of world X/Y high bytes as column/row in a 16-column map. Save old cell, calculate new index=row*16+column, and set map_cell_changed only if the index differs. Bounds are byte wrap, not checked world bounds.

; Twenty four-byte mission map records: CHR bank, little-endian source address and packed start cell (X high nibble, Y low nibble). Warning pointer words and ASCII message strings follow; individual strings retain their exact local bytes.

; Index a 22-byte screen record. Copy 1024 bytes between PPU locations using record bank/source fields, select display CHR and pattern mode, load 16 palette bytes, and enable background rendering. ScreenDescriptorRecords contains twelve complete twenty-two-byte records.

; Twelve twenty-two-byte screen descriptors. Offsets 0/1 select display CHR and pattern mode, offset 2 selects source CHR, offsets 3/4 hold the source PPU address, and offsets 6..21 hold sixteen background colors. Destination is fixed at PPU $2000; offset 5 is not read by this consumer. LoadScreenDescriptor copies a 1024-byte screen before applying palette/rendering state.

; Read a text pointer from CHR bank 15, copy 250 bytes to CPU page $07, select display CHR and interpret the stream. Initial two bytes specify a PPU destination; $fe changes destination relatively and $ff ends. Printable bytes map letters/digits/punctuation to tiles plus a caller bias. Optional typewriter mode plays sound and delays six frames per glyph. Text scratch overlaps OAM staging, so callers control rendering/mode.
; Closed self-loop after the returning text renderer. If entered, it spins without changing registers or the stack. No natural entry is established.

; Save mission index, maintain alternating 16-bit spawn timers, and optionally use mission-20 tables during grace/special state. Limit eligible actor population to fewer than two, apply a random threshold, then select a type from a mission-dependent range; $ff means no spawn. Restore the original mission index before return. Separate counting entry includes active types 1/7/8.
; Request the timed map message and sound, then resume spawn-phase checking.

; Mixed spawn choice lists/counts/bases/probabilities, view sprite/palette pointers, mission objective targets and timer pairs. Existing named aliases identify proven consumer entry points; unresolved subboundaries remain generic data rather than invented records.

; Use mission group (mission & $fc)/4 and alternating phase to select a little-endian timer pair. Following source gaps and uniform non-code blocks remain separately identified; no table bounds are invented.

; Unknown: physical 17039..17040, CPU $c27f. The preceding timer helper returns at $c27e; the supported palette entry begins at $c280. This $60 could be an intentional return stub or obsolete residue; decoding and adjacency do not establish either role.

; Save the X/Y target pointer and A direction. Initialize colors from zero or the target, then adjust low color nibbles and brightness fields over NMI-separated steps until no changes remain. The loop visits offsets $20 down to one, preserving its actual bounds.
; Wait two frames, request palette upload and scan color/brightness differences for the next transition step.
; Continue the descending palette scan; repeat frames until no component changed.

; Palette records followed by pointer-backed twenty-four-byte metasprite frames. Frames use the same eight-column/three-row tile layout and $ff transparency convention. Physical splits preserve older independent classification boundaries.

; Thirty-five zero bytes in the perspective/parameter container. Indexed projection consumers and neighboring ramps were checked; the exact zero-tail meaning remains unresolved, so retain a generic data slice.
; Continuation of pointer-backed twenty-four-byte metasprite payload; existing selector tables establish frame identity. No new actor/game names are inferred from tile appearance.
; Seventy-eight $ff bytes within the scene metasprite container. Shared frame pointers and twenty-four-byte cell records establish the enclosing data layout; $ff cells are transparent.
; Preserved physical slice of the palette/metasprite container. Nearby pointers and repeated twenty-four-byte frame layout establish data; this boundary need not be a logical frame boundary.
; Sixty-eight $ff bytes retained as a physical slice of the scene metasprite payload. The common tile emitter recognizes transparent cells; the slice need not align with one frame.
; Preserved physical slice of the same metasprite container, using byte tile cells and $ff transparency. Exact semantic names of the pictures remain unresolved.
; Thirty-seven $ff bytes in the same scene metasprite payload container. Preserve the exact physical boundary without inventing a new logical record format.
; Metasprite pointer/payload bytes in the established scene graphics container; twenty-four-byte frames are consumed by the common emitter. Physical boundary does not assert a new format.
; Ninety-nine $ff bytes within the pointer-backed interlude metasprite container. Consumer-selected cells use $ff transparency; no picture identity is inferred.
; Pointer-backed scene/interlude metasprite records including the tables selected by the two service interludes. Preserve all selector offsets and shared frame references.

; Separate helpers serialize five low bits to MMC1 control (MMC1_CONTROL_SERIAL) or CHR bank (MMC1_CHR_SERIAL); the first entry doubles the bank selector before serialization. Reset disables rendering, waits for two vblanks, initializes stack to $ef, resets mapper registers, writes control 3 and joins boot initialization. MMC1 serial transactions do not imply permanent execution-bank context.
; Reset entry from vector. The mapper initialization uses the actual serial register protocol.
; Delay X iterations of a 30-count inner loop. X=0 wraps through 256 outer iterations. This is instruction timing, not an emulator frame guarantee.

; Boot configures APU frame mode, PPU/CHR and RAM, initializes audio/random seed/score, draws opening text/screens and enters the title animation. Embedded NMI entry saves A/X/Y, calls the NMI service then restores them before the shared balanced IRQ wrapper returns with RTI. RAM clear covers zero page and pages $02..$07, preserving the active CPU stack page. The classified title/menu tail selects an attract flight or starts a new campaign.
; NMI entry saves foreground registers before servicing frame/audio/render requests.
; IRQ entry preserves/restores A/X/Y and returns with RTI; the NMI path also falls through this balanced wrapper.
; Draw the title screen and return its input/timeout selection to the menu driver.

; Zero menu result starts a timed attract flight on a random mission, saving/restoring the selected mission. The other path initializes a new game, supports the controller-two shortcut to mission nine, shows initial messages and resets lives/score.
; Clear score, set three lives and continue into the mission initialization sequence.

; Reset mission clock, clear ten per-mission counter bytes and ending flag, copy six score digits to backup, then draw the briefing. Artificial entry was tested with a clean cockpit snapshot and mission 19; it does not prove natural progression or an arbitrary-state entry contract.
; Clear the variant latch and show lives, mission-six briefing and any secondary-weapon briefing before the common mission prompt.
; Select sound-only NMI, draw the mission-indexed metatile screen, restore background/NMI and wait 80 frames. Mission briefing and flight setup follow as separate classified entries.
; Wait for fresh controller input before the mission scene setup.
; Display text variant using A=7,Y=9, then wait for release/new input. The connected driver now checks lives/objectives, retries failed missions and advances completed missions.

; Set cockpit sprite parameters, show the departure scene and initialize flight. After flight returns, depleted lives show the summary/score screen. Missing objectives cost a life and retry; success advances the mission and enters completion handling at mission twenty.
; Rebuild cockpit graphics and call the main flight loop again with the current mission state.
; Compare objective_count with the current mission target to choose failure/retry or mission advance.
; Increase the mission index, show the completion prompt and summary, and start the next mission unless the campaign boundary is reached.

; Display text with A=1,Y=16. Artificial execution reached the completion message and subsequent briefing, with transient graphics corruption; this fragment does not establish a naturally reachable ending.
; Wait 150 frames and input, show the completion screen, reset mission to ten and increase the spawn difficulty offset by ten.
; Disable NMI and show the score/name screen before returning to the title loop.
; Closed self-loop between the campaign exit transfer and palette data. If entered, it spins without changing registers or the stack; its intended caller and game purpose remain unknown.
; Sixteen background colors consumed by the screen-palette helper: the four-byte pattern $3e,$3e,$20,$28 repeats four times.
; Load scene nine, seven scripted actors and the special scene palette. Update actors and sound until the signed timer starting at 356 expires, then restore the cockpit tile base.
; Seven actor descriptor selectors for the special-mode exit animation, then two selectors for the base-service interlude. The two finite spawn loops provide the separate lengths.
; Select sound-only NMI and the common clipping/tile conventions for interlude scenes.
; Load scene eight, two scripted actors and its palette. Run the same bounded actor/velocity/sprite animation until the signed 356-tick timer expires.

; Initialize sprite tables, palette and rendering, then move a metasprite right toward X=150 while waiting for a fresh Start edge. Return A=2 for Start and clear a state byte; timeout returns A=0. The controller must first be released to arm the edge detector. The following sprite data has a separate preserved physical boundary.
; Pointer and repeated tile/$ff payload bytes between the title scene and completion helper. Neighboring consumers support sprite data, but a unique exact subrecord layout is not established.
; Load screen eleven and typewriter text sixteen, pause with quiet NMI and wait for fresh input.
; Clear the screen, load descriptor 11, apply the briefing palette and render text in typewriter mode with base tile $e4. The continuation formats the mission number and waits for input.
; Format mission plus difficulty offset plus one at PPU $20f2, then pause for input.

; Load screen eleven and text forty-one. Iterate five six-byte descriptors containing a counter pointer, PPU position and text offset; then show lives-dependent text and two six-digit score quantities before a 200-frame pause.
; Render the lives-dependent summary text, two six-digit score values and the final bounded pause.
; Convert six stored digits to the summary tile alphabet, blank leading zeroes, write at the requested PPU destination, append the zero tile and play a short sound.
; Multiply the 16-bit quantity by ten using shifts and addition; continue into its decimal display helper.

; Format the 16-bit quantity as decimal tiles, translate the tile alphabet and blank leading zeroes. Write the selected buffer slice at the caller's X/Y PPU destination, then play sound fourteen and wait twenty frames.

; Clear 1024 nametable bytes with rendering/NMI disabled and CHR bank 2 selected. Separate palette entries load 16 bytes from the local palette table, wait two vblanks, enable NMI/background and upload colors, resetting address/scroll.
; Replace leading zero tiles with blank tiles in at most five positions and return the count in A.
; As above, but scan up to six digits for score fields.
; Twenty mission bytes. Low seven bits select the reduced ammunition/briefing path; bit seven enables the one-shot randomized actor variant. Callers mask these roles separately.
; Preserve text selector arguments, load screen descriptor 5, choose/render text with a fixed display bank/base, hide sprites, enable background, and pause 80 frames.
; Clear grace/countdown low byte and set countdown high to four ($0400 ticks). This initializes its own A values and does not depend on incoming register contents.
; Zero all six score digits. Later table/gap bytes remain separate and are not decoded by this routine.
; Five six-byte records: little-endian RAM counter pointer, PPU destination low/high, and little-endian offset into the CHR-loaded text buffer. The summary loop advances exactly six bytes per field.
; Unless failure was requested, draw one icon per remaining secondary round at PPU $21c4 onward. Wait fifteen frames and play sound seventeen per icon; preserve the loop count on the CPU stack.
; Preserve remaining ammunition count across its frame wait and draw the next sequential refill icon.

; Sixty-nine low pointer bytes followed by the first high pointer byte of the split actor-script table. The separate high-byte half is consumed with the same selector. Zero is a valid null pointer, not a script root.

; Thirty-eight repeated $f6 bytes in the high-byte half of the sixty-nine-entry split actor-script pointer table. Together with corresponding low bytes, they select validated script record boundaries; this is pointer metadata, not an unexplained fill run.

; Script high-byte pointers, behavior pointers/records and twenty-five three-byte command descriptors. The VM uses the descriptors to choose argument lengths and handler addresses. Exact field aliases identify the individual table starts.

; Separate script commands select the actor behavior-table pointer from a two-byte pointer table, reset the actor software stack, set a yield byte, or free the actor and force a yield. The following entries implement software script return/call.
; Pop the actor's software return pointer and install it as the script pointer. The following entry pushes a return pointer before a script jump/reset.

; Choose initial behavior by mission threshold 10. Preserve interpreter state, allocate a child using the requested descriptor, and on success copy parent position/velocity, add supplied byte offsets, copy behavior metadata and link parent/child slots. Allocation failure jumps to a fallback script address. Offsets add as unsigned bytes with high carry, not signed deltas.

; Commands implement counted loops on the actor software stack, subroutine save/return, and a carry-returning indirect predicate. Predicate target is supplied by script_arg0/1 and caller restores actor X. Different stack-balancing paths discard or recover saved return addresses according to carry. Script validity and stack depth remain caller contracts.

; If a linked actor still has the matching behavior identity, store this actor index with bit 7 set into its backlink. Then clear this actor relationship index to $ff. The intervening packed behavior commands have separate mechanical explanations.

; Interpret argument bits 7/6 as force, toggle or tracked-actor selection and bits 0/1 as destinations. Change behavior polarity and increment frame-change count when the live value is written. Tracked-actor backlink/parent state influences the relative comparison; exact game purpose remains uncertain.
; Write the chosen polarity to one or both behavior fields according to argument bits, updating the live frame-change count.

; Set interpreter and per-actor script pointer from A/Y (or script arguments), reset stream offset, then a separate entry conditionally clears actor state. The connected reset path preserves the interpreter contract and updates actor behavior state.
; Interpreter jump ABI: A/Y carry low/high script address; offset restarts at zero.
; Store the command byte, combine its high bits with the saved behavior sign, and update live behavior/frame-change count only when needed. Continue through the existing behavior-reset path.
; Join the existing behavior-reset decision with the original packed command byte restored.

; Select behavior, reset its software stack, preserve a behavior value, clear velocities/timers and set several optional-link indices to $ff. The cleanup continuation clears all seven actor slots and the tracked-actor index.
; Mark the tracked actor, seven actor states/types and auxiliary slots as free ($ff), then return.
; Mark the slot free ($ff), release its auxiliary allocation and clear the tracked special slot when it matches X. Return leaves other actor fields for future initialization.

; Set type and allocation metadata; establish pending state 2, zero velocities/timers, initialize absent links to $ff, reset stack, select behavior-table and behavior. Allocation failure returns early. Fields without resolved consumers retain neutral mechanical names in operands.

; Find first free slot among seven (X=$ff if none). Read a four-byte descriptor: type, behavior-table selector, packed auxiliary selector, packed frame/lifetime. Initialize the actor, derive packed frame from a lookup and optionally track type zero. Failure restores free status. ActorSpawnFrameDescriptors records the lookup and four-byte descriptors separately from position-based spawn records.
; Store the selected type and return it in X as required by this allocation continuation.

; Spawn frame-index lookup followed by repeated four-byte actor descriptors consumed during allocation: type, behavior selector, packed auxiliary selector and packed frame/lifetime. These differ from the position-based spawn records at $dc25.

; First update scripts for states 0/1, checking relationships and script delay. Then decrement pending states toward active zero, latch behavior/timer metadata and apply queued behavior requests by priority. A nonzero packed frame/lifetime prevents default transitions. This separates execution delay from activation state.

; Resolve a pending behavior or load saved script pointer, then interpret commands until a yield. A high-bit token supplies horizontal velocity from the following byte, then interprets its own low seven bits as the token. Tokens below $67 select frame/family and encode timing/vertical velocity; tokens >=$67 dispatch three-byte command descriptors (handler pointer plus argument count), copying arguments into zero-page scratch. Save advanced stream pointer on yield. Behavior scheduling records a requested ID and priority for later selection.
; Command dispatch: handler low, handler high, argument count; copy that many stream bytes into script_arg0 onward.
; Queue behavior ID from A with priority Y for deferred selection.

; Resolve a behavior selector through the actor behavior table, then use split low/high script-pointer tables. Reset script offset and relationship indices, record active behavior identity, and return. Zero table entries invoke actor-state reset before retrying. A following tiny entry stores X velocity directly.
; Use a nonnegative initial behavior as the stream offset, or zero for a negative value, and read the first selected script byte.

; Per-actor software stack lives in a shared byte arena, with a separate cursor per slot. Push/pop one byte or a two-byte script return pointer, then check bounds. This is independent of the 6502 hardware stack, which is also used temporarily to preserve registers.
; Unknown: Isolated $60 after a terminal actor/script path. No independently established return role excludes non-code residue. Retained verbatim.
; Unknown: Isolated $60 after terminal script-stack control. Preserve it without assigning an additional return entry. Retained verbatim.
; Unknown: Isolated $60 at the software-stack helper boundary. Extra return code and non-code residue remain ambiguous. Retained verbatim.
; Unknown: Isolated $60 at the next software-stack helper boundary. Its opcode value alone does not establish code. Retained verbatim.

; Initialize cursor from per-slot base table. After push compare against the next slot boundary; after pop compare against base and $fb. Invalid ranges route to the descriptor fallback helper rather than proving safe arbitrary scripts. These checks do not prove arbitrary scripts safe; the classified stream has a separately validated record grammar.
; Ten byte boundaries spaced sixteen apart for the software-stack arena. Push/pop use adjacent limits; ten boundary bytes do not imply ten valid actor slots.
; Index a four-byte spawn descriptor: position X/Y are staged into allocation scratch and type/behavior selector returned in A/Y. ActorSpawnDescriptors supplies thirty position-based records.
; Wrap actor-resource cleanup with a normal return. The following entry begins the common actor update step.
; Tick the actor script state machine before continuing into velocity integration.

; For each allocated actor, add signed byte velocities to the low position bytes and increment/decrement high bytes according to sign and carry. Positions use three fractional bits, so velocity units are eighth-pixels per update.
; Jump to the next integration slot for this actor.

; Record an auxiliary selector and initialize split fixed-point X/Y from staged unsigned coordinate bytes by multiplying by eight. Return A=0. Separate entry releases auxiliary selector with $ff. The subsequent departure-scene code has independent entries and temporarily overlays this scratch RAM.
; Auxiliary allocation selector is independent of the seven actor-state slots.
; Return from the preceding actor cleanup entry; no additional effects.
; Thirty four-byte spawn records: descriptor selector, behavior, unsigned X and unsigned Y. The decoder stages coordinates and returns the selectors before actor allocation.

; Read two different CHR-backed scene datasets into the same working RAM, set scene graphics, initialize each animation and run it to its finite end. Shared zero-page actor/flight storage is repurposed as scene timers and coordinates during this sequence.
; Save the scroll/address inputs, load the screen and CHR bank, upload seventeen palette bytes, fill its nametable and initialize animation state.
; Clear elapsed time, scroll and completion state and initialize the next background-write address.
; Capture one background row for later restoration and initialize scene origin, animation counters and sprite timing.
; Clear the secondary animation/origin fields and set the frame countdown to eight.
; Alternate OAM allocation, advance scrolling/timers and draw scene sprites each frame until the completion flag becomes negative.
; Run the second scene's scroll/sprite sequence, request its NMI work and apply scrolling until completion.
; After fifty frames, advance vertical scene scroll by two each update.
; After fifty frames advance vertical scroll by two, while horizontal scroll advances eight per update.
; Increment the little-endian two-byte scene elapsed counter.
; Compare the elapsed counter with A/X and set completion to $ff on equality.

; Draw three staged sprites while their frame timer advances, then animate two four-byte sprite records from an eight-byte paired record stream. Stop each stream when its scrolling threshold is reached.
; After frame thirty-four, animate frame/duration pairs while horizontal scroll is below $a0. A $ff frame marker loops back to byte four.
; Add the scene origin and subtract horizontal scroll, then halve and add $40 for the display X coordinate.
; Apply origin minus vertical scroll, then halve and add $40 for display Y.
; At elapsed frames twenty and fifty, restore the saved row or fill a row with tile two. Reset the PPU address afterward.
; After fifty frames, fill one thirty-tile row with tile $22, apply scene scroll and advance the PPU row offset.
; Write the scene's horizontal and vertical offsets to PPUSCROLL.

; Overlapping departure-scene animation and palette views. One consumer reads paired four-byte sprite records, another frame/duration pairs, and the palette uploader reads a fixed slice. These local formats are established without forcing one exclusive global subdivision.
; Update sound-channel timers and then tick the four music command streams. Called from sound-only NMI mode.

; Stage mission parity and caller X/Y into service scratch, select sound-only NMI and run the service body. The rescue/base caller interprets returned result one as success; service states select arrival, departure or reuse of the current scene.
; Initialize and run the selected rescue/base service, then return its result byte. The loop repurposes shared actor/flight zero-page RAM; callers interpret result one as success.

; State two reuses the current scene. Other states hide OAM, select service metasprites, initialize motion/animation, load the selected screen and palette, and apply rendering before initializing the auxiliary sprite sequence.
; Initialize the auxiliary sprite sequence after the selected screen setup; state two joins here while reusing the current scene.

; Advance the service LFSR helper with the caller's A bound, take the resulting LFSR low bit as direction and select a motion pointer using Y. Save the selector and clear run/delay counters; the unusual helper is not interchangeable with RandomBelowLimit.
; Set auxiliary coordinates to ($d4,$2c), clear its delay and start the auxiliary state machine.
; Clear motion/frame/acceleration state and choose position ($28,$10) for arrival or ($52,$b5) for other service states.
; Clear the main service sprite attributes after choosing its initial position.
; Select attributes and an eight-byte animation descriptor by the saved service selector. Clear stream state and shift initial Y by thirty for nonzero service states.
; Use A as the byte offset of the animation descriptor; copy stream pointer and initial coordinates and reset the stream cursor/timer.
; Load screen six or seven from the service selector, draw its map-dependent strips and upload seventeen palette bytes.
; Choose the rescue/base literal tile stream, apply the mission-dependent horizontal displacement and initialize three collision segments per strip.
; Read the mission's signed strip displacement and motion-stream selector, then update the PPU destination and draw the strip.
; Reverse displacement for the alternate service selector, save its value, adjust the destination pointer and emit the literal tile stream.
; Add signed A to the 16-bit destination. The negative branch uses incoming carry from the low-byte ADC with SBC #0 for the high byte; preserve this exact arithmetic.
; Scale the saved strip displacement by eight and initialize three consecutive horizontal collision segments from nine-byte templates.
; Copy translated left/right limits and the unchanged vertical threshold into one three-byte collision segment.

; Clear result, alternate OAM allocation, dispatch auxiliary state, accelerate and update service motion/animation, then request NMI rendering. Nonzero service states return once Y falls below nineteen; arrival waits for a negative completion bit and strips it from the result.
; Use the even auxiliary-state byte as an index into a word table, load a pointer and tail-dispatch indirectly. State values must satisfy the finite table contract.
; Load the auxiliary callback pointer from its word table.
; Wait sixteen frames before selecting state two; subsequent calls decrement the active delay.
; Decrement the auxiliary state delay and return.
; Set delay five and frame sixteen, mark palette request bits and select state four.
; Animate frames sixteen through eighteen at five-tick intervals. On the last frame, move the auxiliary coordinates toward the main sprite, request the palette change and return to state zero.
; Move one auxiliary coordinate by eight toward the corresponding main coordinate plus its axis offset.
; Transform auxiliary coordinates into display space and emit its frame with attribute one.
; Add $0058 to the split velocity accumulator while its high byte is negative or below twenty-one; stop at the positive threshold.
; Draw the direction indicator, then consume delay/count pairs terminated by $ff. Repeated runs move horizontally by signed sixteen scaled through the common movement helper until Y reaches $b8.
; Reload the inter-step delay and apply the signed horizontal displacement while below the floor bound.
; Select a direction frame from the motion sign and service selector and draw it at the fixed transformed location.
; Dispatch by the result byte through the three-entry result-handler table. This is distinct from the even-index auxiliary-state table.
; Apply input-controlled acceleration and movement, select the animation pose and draw the active service sprite.
; Count down the success delay, then set the completion high bit. Continue drawing the main sprite and advancing its animation.
; Advance failure frames at five-tick intervals until the remaining count reaches zero, then set the completion high bit.
; Draw the main service sprite after advancing its result animation state.
; Scale horizontal velocity and split vertical acceleration, preserving sign flags for the axis helpers, then update both coordinates.
; Save old X; nonzero service states synthesize an Up input, while arrival polls the controller. Dispatch exact controller values through the control callback table.
; Select the exact-input callback table and tail-dispatch its matching acceleration handler.

; Preserve processor flags, complement negative input, divide magnitude by eight and restore flags. Axis helpers consume the original sign; this is one's-complement magnitude, not an absolute-value correction.
; Apply scaled magnitude left or right according to the preserved sign and clamp at 0 or $c0 when already at a boundary.
; Apply the same signed motion vertically, using $10 and $b8 as boundary clamps.
; On even frames move nonzero horizontal velocity one step toward zero.
; Decrease horizontal velocity down to signed -11.
; Increase horizontal velocity up to nine.
; Damp horizontal velocity and subtract $00f0 from vertical velocity down to the negative threshold.
; Apply the upward vertical acceleration portion without repeating horizontal damping.
; Damp horizontal velocity and add $00f0 up to the positive threshold.
; Apply the downward vertical acceleration portion without repeating horizontal damping.
; Combine the left and up acceleration steps.
; Combine the left and down acceleration steps.
; Combine the right and up acceleration steps.
; Combine the right and down acceleration steps.
; Choose direction relative to the saved X and service orientation, add the low-altitude pose bit and toggle its animation phase on a small countdown.
; Return direction code four/eight from old versus new X, reversing interpretation for the alternate service selector; return zero when unchanged.
; Transform main position and emit the current frame, attributes and service-orientation flags.
; Read five-byte duration/frame/dX/dY/flags records, looping at $ff. Accumulate relative position once per record and draw the current animation every frame.

; At the lower boundary distinguish aligned low-speed landing from failure. Success sets result one and selects the next animation; failure starts result two with a three-frame animation. Otherwise test rectangle and bitmap collisions against auxiliary/background geometry.
; Set the failure delay/frame, move Y down eight, select attribute one and result two. This entry may be reached after explicitly unwinding one nested return.
; Return one when the auxiliary coordinate lies inside the main coordinate's forty-unit interval, otherwise zero.
; Resolve the current frame bitmap and test two auxiliary points; combine their hits in work8.
; Transform a point into a coarse frame-cell index and reject outside the two-row bound or transparent $ff cell. Return one for a solid cell and zero otherwise.
; Check three consecutive three-byte collision segments, with each successful test able to enter the common failure path.
; Compare Y with its vertical threshold and X with the half-open left/right interval. A hit pops one return address and transfers directly to failure, skipping the three-segment caller's remainder.
; Inspect the service palette request bits, upload the selected sixteen colors and clear the high request bits. The two branches currently use the same source pointer and destination.
; Retain only the low six service palette bits after uploading the requested colors.
; Convert A to floor(A/2)+$40 in the display coordinate domain.
; Alternate ascending and descending sprite allocation and reset the corresponding hidden OAM tail. The descending limit is the literal byte $56, not a negative decimal value.

; Service data container: nine exact-input value/pointer triples plus $ff sentinel, motion pointers, two independent state-handler tables, tile strips, mission displacements, collision templates, five-byte animation records, palette slices and pointer-backed metasprite frames. Each consumer has its own byte/count/sentinel contract; unrelated selectors must not be interchanged.
; Wait two vblanks, clear scroll and enable the utility screen's direct PPU register settings.
; Enable NMI, disable rendering, hide the entire OAM staging page and DMA it immediately.
; Fill page seven with $ff and copy it to hardware OAM through DMA.
; Write 30 rows of 32 blank tile $ff bytes and then 64 zero attribute bytes at PPU $2000. The following screen-fill helper is classified independently.
; Fill thirty rows of thirty-two tiles using A, then sixty-four attribute bytes using work0. X/Y supply the PPU address low/high bytes.
; Emit bytes below $80 after subtracting $2f. High-bit commands skip forward in the PPU destination; $ff terminates. Streams must terminate within the byte-indexed page.
; Advance the byte cursor after a literal or skip command and continue interpreting the tile string.
; Emit literal tiles; $fe advances the destination by one nametable row and $ff ends the stream. Reset the PPU address at completion.
; Advance the literal-stream cursor after drawing or moving to the next row.
; Subtract $2f from A and draw one tile at X/Y PPU destination.
; Rotate eight bits through carry and emit tile $fd or $fe for each bit. Preserve the original stack balancing and incoming-carry behavior.
; Split A into high and low nibbles, index the hexadecimal character table and draw two biased tiles.
; Scan three-byte value/pointer records until a value equals controller_one (through indexed zero page) or $ff ends the table; tail-dispatch the matching handler.
; Read the next value/pointer triple and compare its key with the requested controller byte.
; Use X/Y as a CPU low/high pointer and write 32 palette bytes to PPU $3f00, then reset the PPU address latch. No palette bounds checking is performed.
; Write X bytes from pointer1 indexed by Y into palette space starting at $3f00+Y; finish by resetting the palette address to $3f00.
; Poll both controllers until their combined button byte is nonzero.
; Wait A vblanks using X as the counter; zero wraps through 256 waits.
; Use X/Y as a CPU pointer and copy exactly 64 attribute bytes to PPU $23c0, then restore PPU address zero.
; Run Y blocks of a wrapping 256-step X countdown. This is a CPU busy delay with no frame synchronization.
; Wait for NMI, write X/Y scroll, force 8x16 sprites in caller-supplied PPUCTRL, and set PPUMASK=$1e. Register values and rendering readiness are caller responsibilities.
; Sixteen ASCII bytes 0123456789ABCDEF used by the nibble formatter; the drawing helper subtracts $2f to obtain the screen tile IDs.

; Load a mission-specific three-byte descriptor (CHR source pointer plus bank), read 240 metatile indices to CPU RAM, then read a $0222-byte six-byte metatile dictionary from CHR. Draw a 16-by-15 grid of 2x2 tile metatiles and accumulate quadrant palettes into 64 attribute bytes. Each dictionary entry has an unused/prefix byte, four tile bytes and packed palette bits. Upload attributes and restore scroll/rendering. Pointer arithmetic computes dictionary_base + index*6; exact full table semantics remain uncertain.
; Screen-load entry: A is descriptor index; this path reuses actor/attribute working RAM.
; Metatile drawing entry: A is metatile index; draw_x/draw_y are tile-pair grid coordinates.
; Resolve record pointer as $04d3 + 6*A; each drawn record contributes four tiles and palette bits.
; Palette accumulation entry; only the high two palette bits contribute, shifted into the selected attribute quadrant.
; Thirty-two palette bytes followed by twenty three-byte mission screen records containing a CHR source address and bank. The mission-screen renderer supplies the record stride and selector.

; Default entry chooses selector 13; main entry reads a four-byte sound request record into frequency/duration/priority scratch, sets octave adjustment four and dispatches the instrument. Instrument descriptors are separate eight-byte records; do not confuse the two formats.
; Sound request fields use the biased base $f17f+4*Y. Selectors 13..23 address SoundRequestRecords at $f1b3 onward; the base itself is not a record and may name executable bytes.

; Resolve the eight-byte instrument descriptor, shift the period according to octave and descriptor adjustment, then choose pulse/triangle/noise channel. Descriptor channel value outside 0..3 returns. The request base is biased; its valid high selectors resolve into the independently classified request records. Channel arbitration uses descriptor priority against current timers/priority values.

; Pulse instrument selects pulse 1 when its channel selector is zero and pulse 2 otherwise; the following priority-aware alternate entry can select an available pulse channel. Each setup path writes its own duration and enable bit.
; Prefer an idle pulse channel; otherwise replace only a channel whose priority timer is below the incoming sound priority. Leave both channels unchanged when neither permits replacement.
; If the corresponding channel is idle or the new priority reaches its current priority, initialize it. Otherwise leave the playing sound intact. Noise has separate short/long-mode entry paths.
; Return from the pulse-one setup path.
; Return from pulse-two setup.
; Return from triangle setup.
; Choose the normal noise-mode setup when idle or when request priority is sufficient. Unknown intervening bytes preserve other audio behavior.
; Return from noise setup.
; Count down X starting at 255 for the first pass and wrapping for the remaining sixty-three Y passes. The inner loop is finite; no natural caller is asserted.

; Separate entry enables all four tonal/noise APU channels. Pulse-one setup records duration, enables the channel, composes duty/envelope/sweep from descriptor fields, and writes the 11-bit period/length registers. Sweep zero selects fixed disabled configuration; nonzero fields encode sweep parameters.
; As pulse one, but use channel-two duration/enable and APU $4004..$4007. Period and descriptor scratch are shared with all instrument dispatchers.

; Triangle setup records duration, enables the channel and sets linear/period registers. A second entry derives the noise-period nibble from the high nibble of the frequency byte and joins common noise setup.
; Derive noise period from the period high nibble and force mode bit $80 before the shared noise setup.
; Record duration and noise enable bit, compose noise envelope from descriptor fields and write length counter. The setup returns through its classified tail.

; Eleven four-byte sound requests for selectors 13 through 23. The selector is biased from $f17f; valid high selectors address these records, not the earlier executable noise setup bytes. Fields are period low/high, tick count and request priority. The original selector separately chooses the eight-byte instrument descriptor.
; Decrease four priority-hold timers and four channel durations. Rebuild APU enable mask from nonzero durations and write $4015, disabling expired channels.
; After decrementing an active priority timer, skip the adjacent zero-timer clearing store and advance to the next three-byte channel record.
; Advance past this channel record after the timer update.

; Resolve note pointer from the current 13-byte channel state. Low nibble zero is a rest. Otherwise read period/octave/duration/instrument; bit $40 ties subsequent notes, accumulating duration from two-byte note records until the chain ends. Store tie state and dispatch the sound instrument. High-bit record commands are handled by the stream reader, not treated as note pitches.
; Music state offsets: +5 active pattern, +6/+7 note pointer, +8 ticks, +9 tie state, +10 instrument.
; Return after initializing the music pattern state.
; Duration lookup bytes followed by little-endian pitch period values. Music note decoding uses separate duration and pitch indices; no continuous waveform interpretation is implied.

; Initialize pattern pointer using a relative offset table plus base. Pattern tick interprets $ff as end, high-bit bytes as instrument changes, and two-byte note records as pitch/duration. Decrement remaining note ticks each update and save the advanced pattern pointer. Carry into pointer high bytes is explicit.
; Visit four 13-byte channel records at CPU $0360,$036d,$037a,$0387 through the shared state pointer and tick each command stream.

; If a pattern is active, tick it; otherwise interpret the channel command stream. Opcode 0 stops; 1 starts a pattern; 2 jumps relative to channel base; 3 loops with a byte counter. Advance stream by opcode-size table when needed, and resume command parsing when a pattern ends. Unknown loop initialization bytes remain preserved, so complete command-3 entry behavior is uncertain.
; Music command state offsets: +0 loop count, +1 pattern, +2 enabled, +3/+4 command pointer, +11/+12 command base.
; Return from this decoded music command handler.
; Read the byte offset following the current command, add it to the per-channel base pointer and replace the command pointer before rechecking stream enablement.
; Read opcode at the current command pointer, add its table-defined length, and store the advanced pointer in channel fields 3/4. Caller provides a valid opcode/table index.
; Four command-length bytes followed by six four-byte initialization pointer records. Channel initialization resolves sequence and pattern bases through these records.

; For the selected music index, load four channel command pointers and bases, plus pattern-offset table and pattern-data base. Mark streams enabled, clear active-pattern and loop counters. Following sequence/pattern data and uniform blocks are separate from this code. Vector words at $fffa select the documented interrupt/reset entries.

; 455 variable-length actor VM records. Frame records carry duration/pose and optional velocity; command records use descriptor-defined argument counts and may carry machine-call or script-branch operands. All sixty-eight non-null split-table roots and explicit branches align to parsed records; this is data for the interpreter, not 6502 code.

; Ninety-seven zero bytes after the validated actor-script stream and before instrument descriptors. No consumer establishes a more specific role; generic data is appropriate without asserting linker padding.

; Twenty-nine eight-byte instrument records. The audio setup consumer derives channel/envelope/sweep/period settings from these fields; following $fc68 bytes are excluded because code/data remains ambiguous.
; Unknown: Bytes $fa,$60 between instruments and the finite PPU loop. A tiny undocumented-opcode helper and data remain competing interpretations. Retained verbatim.
; Write thirty rows of thirty-two copies of A at the X/Y PPU destination. Only this finite loop prefix is classified; the following bytes do not establish a complete returning helper.

; The finite 960-store loop falls through to this load from zero-page $06 (also actor_screen_x slot 6). The loaded value has no established use here. The similar $ebb7 loop instead reads $47; its continuation does not establish this fragment's purpose.

; Clear X after the zero-page load. Finite-loop fallthrough and the corresponding complete LDX in the similar $ebb7 fragment support this instruction; its later use and any complete returning helper remain unresolved.

; Thirty-three zero bytes retained as generic data after the complete LDX. No independently bounded format or subsequent code is established; legal BRK decoding alone does not extend the fill fragment through this run.

; Sparse boundary byte $20 after thirty-three generic zeros and before nine more zeros in the following music container. Music initialization pointers and pattern consumers establish no specific schema for this byte; retain generic data without assigning a music-header or padding role.

; Music command, pattern-offset and note streams selected by channel initialization pointers, together with short zero runs. Command and note interpreters define local lengths and terminators; no single array stride covers the entire container. The interrupt vectors begin separately at $fffa.
; Little-endian NMI/reset/IRQ vectors for this ROM. Values are CPU execution addresses, not physical file offsets.

; CHR backing: 128 KiB in sixteen physical 8 KiB banks. PPU pattern addressing is selected through MMC1 CHR registers. Some consumers read CHR as structured data/text; image classification does not imply every byte is exclusively a visible tile.
